Then from -- before the army there was General Samardzic, the commander of the 3rd Army attended the meeting on the 27th of July. We can see in the minutes that he also took part in the discussion. Then there was also the assistant for intelligence, Colonel Djindjic. And then later on these meetings were also attended by General Lazarevic and a couple of other individuals from the ranks of the army. I think four or five other individuals also began coming to these meetings. As for the Ministry of the Interior, there was General Obrad Stevanovic -- no, he was not present at this first meeting. Then I think on one or two occasions Mijatovic attended. And I don't know if there were any other individuals. So this would be approximately some 20 individuals or so in addition to the names that I mentioned on this first day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me try and jog your memory. I believe that Mr. Matkovic, if I'm not wrong, was also not present at this first meeting.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I did not put down the names of civilians because they were -- they came from time to time, and I think Mr. Matkovic was the minister for the economy at the time. He would come to these meetings occasionally. And there was also an individual, Mr. Milosavljevic, who was in the Executive Council, he was a minister, but he usually did not attend these meetings, although I think that he probably did have some contacts and carried out certain tasks in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you agree with me that all these individuals who were civilians and politicians, that they also had certain state functions in addition to their party roles?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that they all held certain positions in the government. I know that the then-president of the chamber of citizens was there and he was also the director of the railway company, and then there was -- there were also the vice-presidents of the army, Andjelkovic and Matkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, here we frequently heard that these people were party functionaries, but isn't this normal that a party that wins an election would form a government, right, that's normally in any country?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's nothing strange in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, let me now get to the point. Did the army ever carry out or implement any decision by -- issued by the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I consider the Joint Command to be, the decisions exclusively pertained to those decisions that were issued by General Samardzic on behalf of the army. And I stand by this and I'm absolutely certain that General Pavkovic could not carry out any assignment without General Samardzic issuing an -- instructions or being in on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the body or the -- what is being referred to as Joint Command, did it have -- did it include any types -- any elements of command in terms of the army or the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what we refer to as Joint Command actually does not meet any of the criteria that actually applied to commanding, those being, for instance, that the superior officer would establish it by issuing an order; that he would have to determine the organisation and structure of that command and its competences and responsibilities; and also that it would have to be integrated in the system of command of the forces for which that command is being established; and also they would have to determine who would provide support and logistics for those forces. So as far as I know, the corps command never received in any order from the 3rd Army command which defined any of the criteria that I just mentioned. In addition to that it would have to be stamped, and there would have to exist a stamp of this Joint Command, and there would have to be commander of this Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let me ask you this: Would an army unit of any level be able to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters -- the interpreter requests that Mr. Djurdjic repeat his question and the witness repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I will repeat my question and you please give your answer so that we can have it in the transcript. Now, would any military unit be in a position to issue an order to the staff -- to a MUP staff as to the use of MUP units?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And vice versa, could any military unit act on orders from a MUP staff or any other unit of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, unless it was resubordinated, only in those conditions, in both of these cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1998 were there instances of resubordination of units between the army and the military?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now my next question: In view of the complex political situation, most of these events reflected the difficult situation in view of the activities Albanian separatists and terrorists. Now am I correct in saying that the state leadership and the leadership of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia decided to send state persons -- state officials to Kosovo and Metohija who would then together with the military and the police contribute to the resolution of this difficult situation in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that is a normal thing. I think it was a logical thing to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were these meetings where you took minutes under instructions from Mr. Pavkovic, were these meetings in fact -- was the purpose of these meetings to coordinate and inform the state structures, all the government structures, that were working on the resolution of the Kosovo problem?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how I understood them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Speaking about these minutes, am I correct in saying that you only noted down what you considered to be significant for the job at hand that you had as the chief of operations of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part I noted down those -- that information, but I also have to add that Pristina Corps was very much interested in obtaining information from state security organs. These were vital bits of information for our work, and that is why I wrote down in detail the information provided, both by Mr. Gajic and Mr. Radojic [as interpreted]. And almost only 60 per cent of the notes actually relate to that information, that type of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, am I correct that it was General Pavkovic for the most part and sometimes the security organs, in other words, the chief of security when he comes from the Pristina Corps or some other individual, that they would present the security information that they had in the army and that they would brief both the politicians and the MUP members on them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From time to time General Stojanovic provided information to General Pavkovic, and then General Pavkovic would just brief that security organs of the Pristina Corps obtained certain information. And this is what the exchange of information between state security and the Pristina Corps actually amounted to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In view of this large number of people who occasionally attended and took part in these meetings, in the work of these meetings, can we agree that these were individuals who had equal roles and equal standing in this exchange of information and coordination?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, just a brief explanation. Coordination as a rule implies that there is an equal or equitable -- an equitable or equal level of responsibility of all members who participate in it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, we will talk about General Samardzic who was at the time the commander of the 3rd Army. He would present the positions of the 3rd Army at these meetings and give his opinions and suggestions at an equal footing as all the other members -- or participants of the meetings; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, General Samardzic at this meeting, and I have a very vivid memory of it --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, let me stop you there. We will come to this meeting later. There is a document that I would like to show you in relation to that. Just answer my question.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, well my answer is affirmative.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to go back and ask you something about the question that was put by Mr. Hannis, and my question relates to the use of the army. Mr. Hannis told you that according to some members of the military - and I think he mentioned General Perisic and Dimitrijevic - that for the employment of the army, the use of the army, it was necessary to issue a decision on the proclamation of a state of emergency, and the second group in this military leadership considered that such a decision was not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see document D167.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, these are the Rules of Service of the Yugoslav Army. We will see it in a moment on the screens. And I would like now to see Article 473, especially item 2, entitled: "The use of the units in army in peacetime." Would you please just read this to yourself and then we can discuss it together. So Article 473.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I see the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the next page both in the B/C/S and the English versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, are you familiar with this provision?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that this article, 473, governs the use of the Yugoslav Army in peacetime when it involves combatting outlaw, terrorist, sabotage, and other armed enemies?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the army can be used in peacetime for these purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In order to use the army, a decision of the Supreme Defence Council is required as well as an executive decision by the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And after that, in order to use the army shall be issued by the Chief of General Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was this the legal basis for the use of the Yugoslav Army in 1998 in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In compliance with the Rules of Service, it was possible to engage the army in solving these problems as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This paragraph 4 is interesting which says that regardless whether there is an armed rebellion or not, if an army unit is attacked, it has the right to defend itself.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in this situation, no decision is required.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please now look at Exhibit P1226. General, we saw this document yesterday as well. Is it fair to say that despite the plan for combatting terrorist forces and despite the meeting held on the 21st of July, 1998, with the president of the republic, where an order was issued to implement the plan, the commander of the Pristina Corps from the commander of the 3rd Army demands to provide detailed plan or a detailed explanation of their participation in the implementation of the plan?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because there were certain objections and opposition to the plan that was approved with the president of the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Neither the Supreme Defence Council nor the president of the republic nor the body that was set up on the 22nd could order the use of the Pristina Corps, but instead Pavkovic asked the 3rd Army commander to regulate this exclusively.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exclusively.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, in this context let's look -- let's look at document D004-3060. General, when you said "exclusively," that referred exclusively to the army or the commander of the 3rd Army?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was the only one who was in charge. It was possible for General Perisic to issue a direct order to an army commander or the commander of the Pristina Corps and the president of our country under the law, but he can undertake direct command only under exceptional situation and circumstances when he consider that it be necessary. But this should be also known by his subordinate officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is another document dated the 22nd of July. Now we have the commander of the 3rd Army addressing the commander of the Pristina Corps, and he -- regardless of this plan which was approved by the president, he is again asking for a proposal for a direct and indirect engagement of forces.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You're familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you receive it on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move for this document to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00321.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at Exhibit P1227.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You have -- you saw it yesterday, and it was admitted into evidence, but let's establish a link with the previous document. Based on the previous document, did you at the Pristina Corps -- or rather, General Pavkovic draft this document dated the 23rd of July?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was General Pavkovic as a response to the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In which we -- in which he provides a detailed plan of how he intends to use the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the end of the document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This last paragraph we see that General Pavkovic is again requesting approval from the 3rd Army commander for the use of units.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Therefore, without such an approval there could be no such order. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now look at Exhibit P886. It's page 17 in English and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please read the numbers slowly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, now we come to the meeting of the joint --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which number should I repeat? K022-8424, that's in B/C/S and page 17 in English. That's how it was yesterday in e-court. And that's Exhibit P886. Yes, we now have it on our screens. Let's look at the top of the page, also in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It says here that present are General Samardzic and Colonel Djindjic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You told us a while ago that General Samardzic was the 3rd Army commander and Colonel Djindjic was --

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assistant for counter-intelligence and deputy security head of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at page 19 in English and the next page in B/C/S. The English page is wrong. Can we have page 18 in English, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think my learned friend's having a problem partly related to the problem I had the other day. We had initially had in e-court the non-CLSS translation. I moved to substitute the CLSS translation, and he's probably using the one I started out with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: For once, Mr. Djurdjic, you can blame Mr. Hannis for all your troubles.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, no, I'll never do that. Yes, it is indeed page 19 in English and says General Samardzic, but what I see now -- I think that the B/C/S version is all right. Let me just see by comparison where I can find the name Minic. The date is completely wrong in English. I need the 27th of July, and I think that page 17 that I initially requested was the right one. Let's go back because these are completely different numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think in the current version of the English in e-court the meeting of the 27th of July is page number 13, which shows General Samardzic and Djindjic as being present and then pages 14 and 15 are the rest of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Hannis. Let's look first at page 14 in English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, can you tell us what is this discussion about in which General Samardzic is -- has taken to the floor?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that General Samardzic took part in this debate and exchange of information, and I noted down the following. The main goal is Malisevo, and we must not back away. Just a brief comment. General Samardzic knows very well that the Main Staff of the Siptar terrorist forces is in Malisevo, and for that reason he states that regardless of the fact that the plan does not contain an attack on Malisevo and the crushing of these terrorists or the command of these terrorist forces in the vicinity of Malisevo, he ordered that we must not back away. The next bullet, forces should not be thrust from Dulje. Dulje was on the Stimlje-Suva Reka road. And that was one of the key features on this road. I put a question mark for my own purposes for the time when I start planning these activities to include this because I was aware that the army commander was going to ask me if I incorporated his order because that was, and still is, the practice in any military. Malisevo must be crushed. We do not need to hold all the villages, only the key points. The term "crushed" does not involve the literal meaning. It just means occupy or capture. The next point is do not pull out any forces from Junik village because there are main forces there. This term "pull out" means do not activate but keep the forces surrounding them. Next, Troja should be toured with the MUP through Drenovac in order to prevent the spillover of forces. Troja was also one of the important features near the town of Orahovac on the Malisevo-Orahovac road. And since General Samardzic was originally from Kosovo and he exceptionally knew the terrain because he was born in Srbica municipality, the village of Kraljica, he was fully familiar with this territory. And he was not speaking with the aid of map, but based on his good knowledge. And for that purpose he ordered Troja to be bypassed because he didn't expect any losses and any attacks on our forces in that region. Next point, set out again from Blace village and with strong artillery preparations and the strongest possible support. This applies to the area of Blace village, or rather, the road leading from Dulje passage to Malisevo. The next one at 0900 hours, the combat group 243.1 shall begin movement preceded by artillery preparations. So he is ordering the movement and artillery preparation for the combat group 243 in order to -- for it to join the fighting along the axis where its use was planned. So this is what General Samardzic spoke about at the meeting on the 27th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And everything that he said at this meeting, you had to put into practice and to ask approval for this decision from General Samardzic in order for the army unit to comply?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this and the tasks and plans that had already in -- been in existence, prepared a decision and General Samardzic approved it. Officially he approved this decision by this very order, and he also provided written approval.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that not in a single minutes there was any such decision ordered by the command?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, concerning this correspondence between the Pristina Corps commander and the 3rd Army commander, it says the second stage of the plan has been approved, what took place on the 22nd of July. Now tell me, what was the first stage, was it a bringing in of the units?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first stage involved the bringing in of units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means both the MUP and the army units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, when this is mentioned here, this -- there is not a reference to this global plan but to specific implementation plans; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a completely different stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have D176.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But before that, for clarification purposes of the transcript, let me ask you again. Am I correct that the Joint Command never issued any decision and that there is no mention of such a decision in your notes?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, what we see before us is a directive dated the 20th of July, 1998. Are you familiar or were you familiar with this document at the time when it was adopted in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not familiar with this document because this is a directive from the General Staff of the army, and I, as the chief of operations and training, did not receive such directives. I would get an order from the commander of the 3rd Army. So this directive is at the level of the army that is issued by General Perisic to General Samardzic on the basis of which General Samardzic will draft his order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But tell us, please, does it comply with the normal format?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, tell us, please, did you have occasion to review this directive since?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. During the proofing session I saw this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. So this directive - could we now please pull up the next page - provides for the use of the Yugoslav Army. That is under Roman III, engagement of the Yugoslav Army. And could we also see the next page in the English version, please. So on this page we have the first stage. In item 2, General -- paragraph 2, rather --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... it says here -- or rather, could you tell us what does this provide for, this paragraph 2, through quick actions, what does it refer to?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: "Through quick actions coordinated with the forces of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia overwhelm and destroy the sabotage and terrorist forces in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija as per special order from the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's request: Could you please slow down and make pauses between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let us see, under item 2 we have tasks of the 3rd Army; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So do we have an iteration of the same thing as the task of the 3rd Army?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but here it is more specific, and it also specifies which units will be used as reinforcements sent by the General Staff to the corps in order to be able to implement the tasks as envisaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now could we please have D177.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, is this a further development of the directive from the commander of the 3rd Army?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were you familiar with this order?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What were the responsibilities and assignments for the 3rd Corps based on that directive, or rather, this order from the commander of the 3rd Army?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Pristina Corps proceeded to prepare its own decision in keeping with the order of the army commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are all these decisions that we have seen now, were they all already built in, in the plan that had been adopted at the Supreme Defence Council, the global plan, for the suppression of terrorism? So this is in fact this implementation?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact -- in fact, this is the putting into practice of the plan that I described and explained earlier, the three stages provided for there. And here we see in even greater detail the description of the tasks and assignments and the forces that are allocated in order for this task to be implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see D178.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, this is an order by General Samardzic dated 30th July 1998. Tell us, please, were you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document from the army command that we knew of only indirectly because this is an order issued to General Mladenovic for the implementation of this task and he was at the army command, whereas I was at the Pristina Corps. However, when the command came to the barracks, the Kosovski Junaci barracks, we were briefed on this and we provided the report to the army command that we have provided for accommodations and so on. Because we were issued an order to actually provide for accommodations and the establishment of the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, here under item 3 General Samardzic orders that the commander of the Pristina Corps as a member of the Joint Command for KiM shall attend all meetings, and prior to going to meetings he shall acquaint the army Chief of Staff with any possible requests and he shall explain to him the proposals for the engagement of forces with reinforcements. And following his approval he should go to the meeting. After the meeting the commander of the Pristina Corps shall report to the army Chief of Staff on the proposals adopted and those that were provided subsequently which diverge from the proposal, and he shall ask him for permission relating to those requests. He shall inform also the Joint Command for KiM of any decisions concerning these requests. General, is this another proof that the Joint Command could not issue orders and that the army did not take action pursuant to orders from the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And this explicitly provides that an agreement has to be made before the meeting as to what was to be done, and if there are any changes that it has to be sent back to the commander at the IKM and that his approval should be sought for any changes?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The commander issue -- orders General Pavkovic within the framework of the Joint Command. In other words, all questions or all requests that are sought cannot be adopted or approved without his knowledge. In other words, that is explicitly stated there, and this order was in force throughout 1998, which was the time when I usually went with General Pavkovic to brief him -- with General Pavkovic to General Samardzic for briefings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think this would be a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, we're not slow enough. Please try to answer as if you were giving a lecture, and I will be nudged by my assistant to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see D004-2997.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did have opportunity to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This document regulates the briefings of the Chief of Staff of the 3rd Army who was at the forward command post of the 3rd Army; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is an order that daily reports need to be sent; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is stated in paragraph 2, and there is even mention of how long this will be -- how long these reports will take.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the morning briefings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was this document implemented in practice?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I correct that the command of the 3rd Army, or rather, the Chief of Staff received daily briefings on the situation in the field and the activities of the 3rd Corps -- of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please admit this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00322.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see 65 document 01418.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is another request from the commander of the Pristina Corps addressed to the 3rd Army commander in relation to the sending of units of the corps; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And again we see that there is no engagement of Pristina Corps units without the approval of the 3rd Army commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please admit into evidence this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00323.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have 65 ter document 01419.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems vaguely familiar, but I did not -- I was not involved in the implementation of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, but we can't even see who drafted this document, but it is authentic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it is in keeping with the situation as it was developing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, could you explain, please, the heading here says the implementation of the third stage of the plan and then it says "approval." So here again we see that there is a request for approval from the commander of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, in view of the differences in these plans, what did this third stage envisage according to this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it envisaged the lifting of the blockades of these three main roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have -- oh, excuse me, let us first deal with this document, and then we'll see the next one. Could we please admit this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a question I want to raise concerning this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: As he noted, there are no initials of who the author of this document was, and there is no transmission information which makes it different from most of the other documents that we've admitted. So I just raise that as a matter, I suppose it goes to weight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. It has been received, it will be received, but those matters may be relevant to weight.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00324.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or, rather, could we please have D002-4026. Could we blow this up a little bit. Could we enlarge it a bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, could you please mark, if you can of course see well enough --

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can manage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher to please assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, as far as I understood your testimony, there were three main roads that needed to be deblocked. Could you please show us and indicate what they were.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first road was the road between Kosovska Mitrovica via Rudnik, Mount Rudnik, the municipality of Istok, towards Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put a number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you please indicate the second road or major communication.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second road leads from Pristina via Glogovac, Klina, and then here it forks into two sub-roads, one goes towards Pec and the other one goes toward -- the other fork goes to Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you put a number 2 where the fork is.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the third direction?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third road leads from Stimlje via Dulje, Suva Reka, to Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you mark this with a number 3.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please admit this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00325.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, do you recall whether for the implementation of this third stage any operations were ordered and executed, if any, and what kind of decisions were made?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember for the most part, which is only natural, because those -- this was the most important stage in the implementation of the plan. May I use the map and mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, no, we shall have a new map for this purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have again Exhibit D002-4026. And can we have it enlarged again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, please.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along this first road or axis number 1, the fiercest resistance was put up in the area of Mount Rudnik. This is this part here. There were exceptionally strong forces there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you please put number 1 in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within this axis and in the area encompassed by the villages which are within this circle, there are quite a few villages and they have Siptar or Albanian names, so it is a little bit difficult for me to decipher them, although I know some of the villages like Vocnjak and other but I'm not sure about all of them. So this is number 2. Then the next area is on the approaches to Pec and the villages between Klina and Pec, and that's number 3, that's this axis. And the major stronghold was west of Pristina near Iglarevo village, including all these villages, and this whole area was totally occupied. They had strong features and they included all these villages. This is a densely populated area and practically this whole area was occupied. We found bunkers made of reinforced concrete when we managed to open up a passage here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, can you please make this number 4.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next, the area between Pec along these roads from Decani and the area of Glodjane and Baranski Lug, it is not even necessary to make these circles because there was so many armed men in Metohija that it was totally incredible. Unlike the eastern line Pristina-Urosevac where these numbers were significantly lower. Then next Kranovica [phoen] all the way to Pec was totally occupied, this is number 5 and this is number 6. Next, via Malisevo and Troja, all the way to Orahovac --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: For the sake of transcript, let us say, General, 1, 2, 3 is the first axis from the previous one, and 4, 5, 6, are ... ?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's another axis, but only this sub-axis from Glogovac via Malisevo and Orahovac was the one mentioned by General Samardzic transversing [as interpreted] Troja. That was the main headquarters of the Siptar terrorist forces in the village south-east of Malisevo. I think the name of that village where their command was Dragobilje. That was their main command for all their forces. Next, this would be 7. The next one leads from Stimlje to Dulje. That's number 8, another stronghold. Number 9 covers the area around Suva Reka and includes the villages south-east of that region. That's number 9. I'm not including here the areas that are west of Pec, Djakovica, and Prizren because the whole road from Pec via Decani, Djakovica, and Prizren was totally blocked and MUP suffered most losses in this particular area, especially near Decani. I remember an incident when 12 policemen were killed at once near Decani, were either wounded or killed in clashes with the terrorists, and that took place in one day alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So numbers 8 and 9 indicate the third axis.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00326.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see Exhibit D003-2618, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, are you familiar with this document dated the 1st of August, 1998?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a document sent by the 3rd Army commander to the Pristina Corps command?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was the decision of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are kindly asked to pause between questions and answers. It is impossible to interpret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have to stop, I'm afraid, General. Your answer is far too quick on the question. The interpreter could not finish the question before your answer was well advanced. So if we go back to the end of the question and then ask the general to answer again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, this is an order issued by the 3rd Army command to the commander of the 3rd -- or the Pristina Corps concerning Joint Command; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you comment this decision made by the 3rd Army commander?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 3rd Army commander forbids the use of the units of the Pristina Corps with reinforcement who are engaged in Kosovo and Metohija pending the approval of the plan for the execution of the third phase of the operation in Kosovo and Metohija, 3rd of August, 1998, at 1300 hours, in a meeting with the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and his previous approval of the 2nd of August, 1998, at the command of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this indicate that the Joint Command did not have any function in terms of issuing orders or instructions --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's asking the witness to make a legal conclusion that I think is for Your Honours at the end of the case when you've heard all the evidence. I object to the form of the question. There was an earlier one about that. There was an answer yes, before I could even hear the translation. So I want to be on record that I'm opposing these kinds of questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The question that you are putting is one which applies reasons and infers conclusions that may or may not be justified by what is said here, and you are not asking them of the knowledge of the witness but simply for his commentary on the document. So your question is going too far there, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I was not referring to the legal aspect. I was talking about the factual situation and the relationship between the army command and the Pristina Corps and the body that was called the Joint Command. I know of course that you are the only ones who can draw legal conclusions, but anyway, I'm thankful to my learned colleague for drawing my attention to this issue. I would like to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00327.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see the document 65 ter number 04045, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, are you familiar with this format of reporting by the security organ of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with the format.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 3 it says that: "Women and children have fled from Junik as have a number of terrorists who abandoned their weapons and went to the Republic of Albania or into the interior. There are now about 700 terrorists in Junik." Did you have any information or report about these claims at this period of time, which is the 1st of August, 1998?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, at the end of this first page in B/C/S - and that would be on page 2 in the English version - it reads: "Reliable sources from the Glogovac area have said that the civilian population has been evacuated from the villages of Prekaz, Laus, Poljance, and Poluza ..." Do you know who organised and carried out the evacuation of civilians?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to see the date of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's the 1st of August, 1998. You can see it on the top of the page, and this is the bottom of the page that I'm reading from.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to say for this particular sector who carried out the evacuation of the civilian population, but in principle if there are combat operations in progress, the commander of a brigade -- it is his duty to evacuate the population from the area of combat operations. That's one solution. But what happened in most cases was that the Siptar terrorist forces would send the civilians on the move immediately prior to any major attacks on the MUP and the army and would send them out as refugees and thereby created a situation which resembled the expulsion of the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00327 -- 328. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look 65 ter document 04051, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but just let me read through it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you comment on it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army commander still forbids the use of army units with reinforcements, except for the purpose of securing the state border and possibly repelling attacks on the army personnel and installation, which means only in exceptional cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Under item 4 there is a request for daily reports to be provided by the commander of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and in addition to that he should receive a written combat report from the Pristina Corps command on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have this document admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00329.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at Defence Exhibit D213.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, this is an order dated 7th of August, 1998. I'm interested in this item 2 that's been highlighted by someone. And in relation to the previous document has anything changed here within these few days, or is the 3rd Army command now allowing the use of forces in concert with MUP forces?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Give me a minute, please. Yes, the situation changed. It took place on the 7th, and the army commander hereby orders for support to be provided to the MUP forces from the deployment area in which the VJ units are stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see 65 ter document number 01422.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, this is an order issued by the Pristina Corps on the 7th of August, 1998. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have page 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document was drafted by my assistant Ratko Tesevic; he worked on it. And if we can go back to page 1 now. Yes, in compliance with this order of the commander of the army he did this, but it included the ban on inflicting damage on persons and property, and it involves specific measures and orders issued to commanders relating to the protection of property of the Albanian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, General, but in the preamble there is an assessment that it was done in a highly professional manner and with good assessment these actions had been carried out; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have this document admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00330.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have Defence Exhibit 004-3006.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, this is a regular combat report of the forward command post of the 3rd Army dated 9th of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And in it under item 3, if we can please see item 3 in both languages, it is said that: "Part of the Army forces are providing support to MUP forces in accordance with the decision on engagement." And then it goes on to say on which axis. Therefore, there is no mention about any problems in functioning between the Pristina Corps and the army command.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at item 5, and it's on the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Here we see the decision in paragraphs 2 and 3. It says continue to support MUP forces which is in line with the previous approved use of the units.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have this document admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D00331.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, these combat reports from the forward command post of the 3rd Army, are they in any way related to the third stage of the implementation of the global plan, and were they -- within this third stage, did they also comprise a decision on routing the DTS forces, sabotage and terrorist forces, in the area of Slup and Voks, Slup and Voks?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are related -- they do relate to that, but we have to stress that the plan as it existed could not envisage all the scenarios that would develop in a period of a several months so that some actions had to be repeated on a number of times in some areas, especially in Glodjane and Baranski Lug because this was an area which had a lot of problems and the commander had to approve a new plan every time because what would happen is we would neutralise certain points, but these targets would re-emerge seven or eight days later. So that as a matter of course, this would be a standard report provided from the command of the Pristina Corps, which would then be forwarded to the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have Defence Exhibit 004-3062.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, are you familiar with this decision as it is plotted on this map?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already answered the question put by the Prosecutor -- by the Prosecutor, and I said that I knew that this was approved personally by the general of the army. But I did not see this particular map as presented here, but rather the plan drafted by the army commander, and it included a number of activities, whereas this is an excerpt from that portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But could you now please see what it says below, it says Samardzic Dusan and there is a signature there. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can, but I don't know where the signature of General Samardzic came from on this particular map. This is not something that is clear to me. I know that this plan was approved for the general area of Pec, Voksa, Slup, and Decani. But why this was individually signed, why -- well, perhaps the general signed off on these individual plans, maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. But the signature that we see here, can you recognise it as the signature of General Samardzic in the upper left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, General Samardzic is the responsible individual here and also General Pavkovic's signature. But I cannot say with certainty that that is so, that these are their signatures. But I can only say that I know for a fact that this action was approved by General Samardzic; of that I am sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see D004-3052 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you move on, I believe the map that the witness has just spoken about is already an exhibit. Could we have the exhibit number for the transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that, I believe, was given Exhibit Number P1237.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. My assistant noted this or informed me that this has already been admitted, and that is why I did not ask for its admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, we see here a regular combat report provided by the forward command post of the 3rd Army, and it was compiled on the 14th of August. Could we now see item 5, please. That would be on page 4 in English. And in the B/C/S version that's on page 3. General, in paragraph 2 under item 5 we can see that Combat Group 15-3 still provides support to MUP forces.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The command of the army, and then proceed in the same manner. So we see that, again, there is no problem now -- there is no problem mentioned here between the Pristina Corps and --

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, there is no mention of such a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we admit this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00332.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see document D004-2953.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, this is an order from the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, dated 17 August 1998. And we see here in the preamble that it says that in the period between the 13th and 15th of August, 1998, a tour of inspection of part of the commands and units of the 3rd Army was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now move to the next page, item 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, could you comment on this item 4 of the document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of this. After this tour of inspection we were issued very specific tasks by the Chief of Staff of the 3rd Army, and we actually translated them into an order for the Pristina Corps. One of them -- one of those orders was to prevent the spilling over of part of the sabotage and terrorist forces from the KiM territory in the area of Raska-Polim which means to the north-west of -- in the north-west of Kosovo as well as the area of the Jablanica and Juzna Morava district which is the area towards Vranja and Leskovac. And to coordinate a joint action with MUP forces. And in keeping with assessments, support MUP forces in destroying the DTG groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, after this tour of inspection there were no objections made either to the 3rd Army or to the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the Chief of the General Staff was there in person with a strong team, and from these assignments we can see that the assignments were actually carried out according to plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D0333.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now pull up document D004-2965.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, I believe that a few moments ago you mentioned this document, but here we see that this was a document produced by the army command following the -- a report after the inspection. And I would especially like to refer you to item 4 which is on the next page.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command system is operational, functioning well, both vertically from the Pristina Corps to the General Staff and the other way around, from the General Staff to the Pristina Corps and the subordinate units, which is affirmed by this order issued by the army commander pursuant to an order from the Chief of the General Staff which we had occasion to see earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see page 2. Yes, I see it now on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you comment on items 4 and 5, paragraphs 2, 4, and 5.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here we see the implementation of this item, and it says that in cooperation with the command of the 2nd Army and in coordinated action with MUP forces and the deployment of forces in the area, the spillover of DTS should be prevented from the KiM area -- the spillover from the KiM area into the Raska-Polim district and into the Jablanica and Cinja [as interpreted] district should be prevented. And the responsible bodies are the army command which means it -- it's own command and the Pristina Corps command. And this is a continuous task which is very important.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00334.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see Defence Exhibit 004-2987.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, this is -- these are minutes from the briefing of the commander of the IKM, and you attended this briefing?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You've already mentioned this, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the next page in the B/C/S version, which is page 5 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We see here -- is this a reference to you, PrK NOOPiO?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So this is your discussion; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And this is in preparation for Operation Ratis; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: On the next page, and that's the end of the document, and it's on the last page of both versions, the 3rd Army commander approves the decision of the PRK commander for the Ratis operation and concludes his reporting; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00335.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have D004-3063. I may be mistaken, but then again maybe not, but when we see it on the screens we'll know if this is the right document. It's again a reference to Ratis operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is this the same map, General, that we saw a little earlier or not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen it yet. It's not on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It will be in a moment. It says Ratis village, and we can now see the signature, it's clearer.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the signature of General Samardzic is far easier to make out now. And, again, this is done in the way that he normally did it, by signing it in a felt-tip pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So is this the same map?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were many plans for certain -- for actions, but this one is produced on the basis of the plan, which is the normal way to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you this: Did the army commander sign off on the excerpts which we don't have here before us, or did he only sign off on the -- let me put it in layman's terms, a general, basic plan?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the thing, I know that that plan was approved. But how these were approved, I'm not clear on that. Whether they were taken to the commander individually, whether that's what he demanded, I don't know, it could be that he would not allow a single operation without his approval.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I apologise, but you are in fact in charge of preparing these decisions and translating them into maps; in other words, they were made pursuant to your orders?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. When General Pavkovic was at the IKM, I took this plan for approval to the general, the plans for Voksa and Slup, the operations that were carried out in the area between Decani and Pec. Now, how it came about that these decisions were signed -- because based on what I see here, this is an original signature. But whether General Samardzic asked General Pavkovic to provide individual excerpts for his signing, I don't know, but that's what it seems to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But just tell me: Is this an original signature?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can see, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00336.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That appears to be a convenient time, Mr. Djurdjic. We therefore adjourn and will continue tomorrow at 2.15.
